title: Fiverr vs Upwork for Hiring a Video Editor
h1: Fiverr vs Upwork for hiring a video editor
description: How hiring a video editor works on Fiverr and on Upwork, which suits one-off edits or ongoing work, what our video editing picks charged, and what to check.
intro: Fiverr and Upwork are the two marketplaces most creators and small businesses look at when they need a video editor. They work differently: on Fiverr you mostly choose from ready-made packages, while on Upwork you usually post a job and compare proposals. This article explains the difference and when each one tends to fit better.

faq.a: It depends on the editor, not the platform. Both have budget and premium editors. Both also add fees for buyers at checkout, so compare the final total.

faq.q: Can I hire an editor by the hour on Fiverr?
faq.a: Fiverr is mainly built around fixed packages and custom offers. Upwork is commonly used for hourly contracts.

faq.q: Which is better for a weekly YouTube channel?
faq.a: Either can work. Many creators test editors with one video, then keep the best one on a regular arrangement on the same platform.
Yes. Some people use Fiverr for quick, defined edits and Upwork for longer roles. Keep each project on the platform where it started.

faq.q: Should I pay an editor outside the platform?
faq.a: No. It removes the order record and dispute options and breaks both platforms' rules.
